findings: 2026–2027 Appendix I and Arts. 3.6–3.10 verify 180 EC: 20 EC core courses, 5 EC core lab skills, 5 EC core project, 10 EC restricted general education, 70 EC profile courses, 20 EC skills, 20 EC projects and 30 EC thesis. No formal route to select. Catalogue P1 pairs chemistry and physics with PRA1101, P2 pairs biology and science philosophy with PRA1102. PRO1101 applies these through literature review and a poster. The accessible linked archival catalogue is dated 2025–2026 and establishes course content, while the formal requirements use the 2026–2027 EER.

The standard electives include at least 20 EC of advanced courses, 5 EC of advanced skills, and 5 EC of advanced projects. Introductory elective ceilings are 15, 5 and 5 EC respectively. The non-minor pathway requires 90 EC from the MSP catalogue itself and 120 EC from it plus its appendix, excluding the thesis from the latter minimum. The final-semester thesis requires 145 EC, of which at most 12.5 EC and a project may still be under grading; at most one module may run alongside it. Open choices remain subject to module prerequisites. The catalogue lists the uncredited MSP1000 introduction as a prerequisite for the core lab skills.

The closest plan sustains life science through molecular cell biology, metabolism, genetics and laboratory experiments, and Earth systems through geology, biogeochemistry, climate, spatial analysis and Earth system modeling. Marine Biology and Earth Observation give field and spatial methods in place of the unsuitable early research-project offering and broaden ecosystem evidence in place of physiology. The neuroscience option prioritises brain, cognition, language and biomedical function; statistics and evidence synthesis support its methods. The quantitative life-science option prioritises signals, numerical analysis, imaging and machine learning as transferable methods alongside physiology and molecular biology, with no implied specialist bioengineering qualification. Sustainability Essentials I covers real physical, chemical and materials concepts in applied contexts; Biochemistry and Environmental Biogeochemistry extend chemistry in selected domains. Neither sustained disciplinary chemistry/physics nor a materials-science pathway is supported. Core chemistry correspondence is partial and introductory physics, philosophy of science and the collaborative core project have no adequate one-to-one counterparts. General education and profile choices are kept open. Optional independent research does not count toward 180 scheduled EC.
